title: Synthetic Commercial Loan Agreement (One-Sided)
summary_en: This document is a commercial loan and credit facility agreement governing a term financing arrangement between a commercial lender and a borrower. Its primary purpose is to provide an INR 1,500,000 credit facility for business capital, subject to stringent repayment schedules, substantial prepayment exit fees, and unlimited personal guarantor liability. Because five out of the seven clauses contain severely restrictive stipulations—including retroactive compound penal interest, unilateral interest rate adjustments, and immediate acceleration without cure—the contract presents an exceptionally high level of financial and operational risk.
summary_hi: यह दस्तावेज़ एक वाणिज्यिक ऋणदाता और एक उधारकर्ता के बीच एक अवधि वित्तपोषण व्यवस्था को नियंत्रित करने वाला एक वाणिज्यिक ऋण और ऋण सुविधा समझौता है। इसका प्राथमिक उद्देश्य व्यावसायिक पूंजी के लिए एक आई. एन. आर. 1,500,000 ऋण सुविधा प्रदान करना है, जो सख्त पुनर्भुगतान अनुसूची, पर्याप्त पूर्व भुगतान निकास शुल्क और असीमित व्यक्तिगत गारंटर देयता के अधीन है। क्योंकि सात खंडों में से पांच में गंभीर रूप से प्रतिबंधात्मक शर्तें हैं-जिनमें पूर्वव्यापी चक्रवृद्धि शास्ति संबंधी ब्याज, एकतरफा ब्याज दर समायोजन और उपचार के बिना तत्काल त्वरण शामिल हैं-अनुबंध एक असाधारण रूप से उच्च स्तर का वित्तीय और परिचालन जोखिम प्रस्तुत करता है।
summary_ta: இந்த ஆவணம் ஒரு வணிகக் கடன் வழங்குநருக்கும் கடன் வாங்குபவருக்கும் இடையிலான ஒரு கால நிதி ஏற்பாட்டை நிர்வகிக்கும் வணிகக் கடன் மற்றும் கடன் வசதி ஒப்பந்தமாகும். கடுமையான திருப்பிச் செலுத்தும் அட்டவணைகள், கணிசமான முன்கூட்டியே செலுத்தும் வெளியேறும் கட்டணங்கள் மற்றும் வரம்பற்ற தனிப்பட்ட உத்தரவாதக் பொறுப்பு ஆகியவற்றிற்கு உட்பட்டு வணிக மூலதனத்திற்கு ஒரு ஐ. என். ஆர் 1,500,000 கடன் வசதியை வழங்குவதே இதன் முதன்மை நோக்கமாகும். ஏனெனில் ஏழு பிரிவுகளில் ஐந்து கடுமையான கட்டுப்பாட்டு விதிமுறைகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளன-இதில் முந்தைய கூட்டு அபராத வட்டி, ஒருதலைப்பட்ச வட்டி விகித மாற்றங்கள் மற்றும் குணப்படுத்தாமல் உடனடி முடுக்கம் ஆகியவை அடங்கும்-இந்த ஒப்பந்தம் விதிவிலக்கான உயர் அளவிலான நிதி மற்றும் செயல்பாட்டு அபாயத்தை வழங்குகிறது.

flagged_clauses.title: Acceleration of Loan
flagged_clauses.original_text:
Clause 3. Immediate Loan Acceleration Without Cure
Upon the occurrence of any technical breach or delay, the Lender shall have the unconditional right to declare
all future unmatured principal and interest immediately accelerated, due, and payable in full without providing
any prior cure period, formal demand, or legal notice.
flagged_clauses.explanation: This clause allows the lender to immediately accelerate and demand full payment of all future unmatured principal and interest upon any technical breach or delay. It explicitly excludes any requirement for prior notice, formal demand, or a cure period.
flagged_clauses.risk_reason: The clause exposes the borrower to sudden, total loan recall over minor or technical non-compliance without an opportunity to rectify the issue. This creates substantial financial vulnerability by removing standard notice and cure protections.

flagged_clauses.title: Guarantor Liability
flagged_clauses.original_text:
Clause 6. Unlimited Continuing Guarantor Liability
The Guarantor undertakes an unlimited, irrevocable, and continuing personal guarantee for all present and
future obligations of the Borrower, authorizing the Lender to seize, attach, and liquidate the personal and family
assets of the Guarantor immediately upon default without first initiating recovery proceedings against the
primary Borrower.
SYNTHETIC DEMO DOCUMENT - NOT A REAL CONTRACT
flagged_clauses.explanation: This clause establishes an unlimited, irrevocable, and continuing personal guarantee covering all present and future obligations of the borrower. It also allows the lender to immediately seize and liquidate the guarantor's personal and family assets upon default without first pursuing the primary borrower.
flagged_clauses.risk_reason: It imposes unbounded financial liability on the guarantor and permits direct enforcement against personal and family assets without exhausting remedies against the primary borrower. This exposes the guarantor to immediate asset liquidation for debts they did not directly incur.

flagged_clauses.title: Penal / Default Interest
flagged_clauses.original_text:
Clause 2. Compound Penal and Default Interest
If any scheduled installment or interest payment remains unpaid for more than twenty-four (24) hours following
its due date, a compound penal interest rate of 36% per annum shall be applied retroactively to the entire
original principal facility sum from the date of initial disbursement until complete settlement.
flagged_clauses.explanation: This clause specifies that if any payment is overdue by more than 24 hours, a compound penal interest rate of 36% per annum applies retroactively to the entire original principal amount. The penalty runs from the date of the first disbursement until full settlement.
flagged_clauses.risk_reason: Applying an extreme penal interest rate retroactively to the entire original facility rather than solely to the overdue amount creates substantial financial liability for a very brief delay. It exposes the borrower to compounding costs across the entire loan balance even if prior installments were made on schedule.
flagged_clauses.explanation_hi: यह खंड निर्दिष्ट करता है कि यदि कोई भुगतान 24 घंटे से अधिक समय से अधिक समय से बकाया है, तो 36 प्रतिशत प्रति वर्ष की चक्रवृद्धि शास्ति संबंधी ब्याज दर पूर्वव्यापी रूप से पूरी मूल मूल राशि पर लागू होती है। शास्ति पहले संवितरण की तारीख से लेकर पूर्ण निपटान तक चलता है।

statutory_provisions.title: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for
statutory_provisions.text: 74. Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for.—When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for. Explanation.—A stipulation for increased interest from the date of default may be a stipulation by way of penalty. Exception.—When any person enters into any bail-bond, recognizance or other instrument of the same nature, or, under the provisions of any law, or under the orders of the Central Government or of any State Government, gives any bond for the performance of any public duty or act in which the public are interested, he shall be liable, upon breach of the condition of any such instrument, to pay the whole sum mentioned therein. Explanation.—A person who enters into a contract with Government does not necessarily thereby undertake any public duty, or promise to do an act in which the public are interested.

The Borrower shall not prepay, foreclose, or refinance the outstanding loan prior to scheduled maturity without
paying an mandatory exit penalty of 12% of the original sanctioned loan facility, in addition to all unaccrued
interest projected through the full original tenure.

28.Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void.—Every agreement,— (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto, from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to the extent. Exception 1.—Saving of contract to refer to arbitration dispute that may arise.—This section shall not render illegal a contract, by which two or more persons agree that any dispute which may arise between them in respect of any subject or class of subjects shall be referred to arbitration, and that only the amount awarded in such arbitration shall be recoverable in respect of the dispute so referred. Exception 2.—Saving of contract to refer questions that have already arisen.—Nor shall this section render illegal any contract in writing, by which two or more persons agree to refer to arbitration any question between them which has already arisen, or affect any provision of any law in force for the time being as to references to arbitration4. Exception 3.—Saving of a guarantee agreement of a bank or a financial institution.—This section shall not render illegal a contract in writing by which any bank or financial institution stipulate a term in a guarantee or any agreement making a provision for guarantee for extinguishment of the rights or discharge of any party thereto from any liability under or in respect of such guarantee or agreement on the expiry of a specified period which is not less than one year from the date of occurring or non-occurring of a specified event for extinguishment or discharge of such party from the said liability. Explanation.—(i) In Exception 3, the expression "bank" means— (a) a "banking company" as defined in clause (c) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949(10 of 1949); (b) "a corresponding new bank" as defined in clause (da) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949(10 of 1949); (c) "State Bank of India" constituted under section 3 of the State Bank of India Act, 1955 (23 of 1955); (d) "a subsidiary bank" as defined in clause (k) of section 2 of the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959(38 of 1959); (e) "a Regional Rural Bank" established under section 3 of the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976(21 of 1976); (f) "a Co-operative Bank" as defined in clause (cci) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949(10 of 1949); (g) "a multi-State co-operative bank" as defined in clause (cciiia) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949(10 of 1949); and (ii) In Exception 3, the expression "a financial institution" means any public financial institution within the meaning of section 4A of the Companies Act, 1956(1 of 1956).

statutory_provisions.title: Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence
statutory_provisions.text: 19A. Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence.—When consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. Any such contract may be set aside either absolutely or, if the party who was entitled to avoid it has received any benefit thereunder, upon such terms and conditions as to the Court may seem just.

flagged_clauses.title: Unilateral Interest Rate Change
flagged_clauses.original_text:
Clause 5. Unilateral Interest Rate Adjustment
The Lender reserves the sole, unilateral, and unreviewable authority to increase or alter the interest rate at any
time at its discretion, without benchmark linkage or advance notification, and the Borrower waives all rights to
contest or challenge any revised repayment schedule.
flagged_clauses.explanation: This clause allows the lender to modify or increase the interest rate at any time at its sole discretion without prior notice or reference to an external benchmark. It also requires the borrower to waive all rights to challenge or contest any revised repayment schedule.
flagged_clauses.risk_reason: This provision creates significant financial uncertainty by enabling arbitrary increases to borrowing costs without advance warning. Additionally, it eliminates the borrower's ability to dispute revised terms or adjust to the modified financial burden.

flagged_clauses.typical_phrasing_disclaimer_ta: இது இந்தப் பிரிவின் பொருளை விளக்குகிறது. இது சட்ட ஆலோசனை அல்ல. இதன் அடிப்படையில் செயல்படுவதற்கு முன் ஒரு வழக்கறிஞரைக் கலந்தாலோசிக்கவும்.
standard_alternatives: Interest rates shall vary strictly in accordance with published changes in the Reserve Bank of India repo rate or external benchmark benchmarked transparently.
Any modification to the floating benchmark rate shall be notified to Borrower 30 days in advance with the option to prepay the loan without penalty if unaccepted.
The applicable interest rate shall be pegged to the standard Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate (MCLR) published quarterly by the banking regulator.
Changes to the margin spread shall require mutual written consent, while the benchmark rate shall adjust automatically to regulatory market movements.
